title: Cotangent homology of a complete-intersection fraction field
statement: Let $k,K$ be fields with a $k$-algebra structure on $K$, $n\ge0$, $P=k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ a regular sequence in $P$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Put $I=(f)$ and $A=P/I$, and assume $A$ is a domain. Given a $k$-algebra isomorphism $e:\operatorname{Frac}(A)\cong K$, there exists a $K$-linear map $\delta:K^c\to K^n$ with $K$-linear isomorphisms $H_1(L_{K/k})\cong\ker\delta$ and $\Omega_{K/k}\cong K^n/\operatorname{im}\delta$. The cotangent objects are those of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; the fraction field is localization at all nonzero elements [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Tag 07E1 (lemma-cartier-equality), the displayed two-term complex and the reference to Algebra Tags 00S1 and 00S7.

proof.text: Write $c=\operatorname{length}(f)$ and $\alpha:P\twoheadrightarrow A$ for the quotient. The classes of $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ give an $A$-basis of $I/I^2$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free]. The polynomial differentials $dX_i$ give a $P$-basis of $\Omega_{P/k}$ and hence a base-changed $A$-basis of $A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/k}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis]. In these bases the conormal differential $g\bmod I^2\mapsto1\otimes dg$ is an $A$-linear map $\delta_A:A^c\to A^n$ with entries $\alpha(\partial f_j/\partial X_i)$. The kernel and cokernel of the differential are therefore isomorphic to those of $\delta_A$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E1, lines 8584-8590 (the displayed complex; I/I^2 free on the f_j by Algebra Lemma 00LN since the f_j form a regular sequence)

proof.text: The exact conormal sequence [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] is $I/I^2\to A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/k}\to\Omega_{A/k}\to0$. Its middle map is the same conormal differential, so $\Omega_{A/k}\cong\operatorname{coker}\delta_A$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E1 (H_0 of NL is Omega, Algebra Section 00S0)

proof.text: For the first homology, use [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] to identify the complex of the canonical presentation $k[A]\to A$ with the canonical naive cotangent complex. Lift each polynomial generator of $P$ to its image variable in $k[A]$, and lift every $a\in A$ to a representative in $P$. These define morphisms of presentations in both directions, over the identity of $k\to A$. By presentation functoriality [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality], any two such morphisms induce the same map on $H_1$, and the maps of identity and composition are identity and composition. The two induced maps on $H_1$ are thus inverse. It follows that $H_1(L_{A/k})\cong\ker\delta_A$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy, line 35274), (1), (2) and the final assertion (comparison with the canonical presentation), cited in the proof of More on Algebra 07E1 line 8590

proof.text: Let $S=A\setminus\{0\}$ and $F=S^{-1}A$. Exactness of localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] applied to the kernel and cokernel sequences of $\delta_A$ identifies the localized kernel and cokernel with those of $\delta_F:F^c\to F^n$. The comparison theorems [lem-weil-pbc-h1-cotangent-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identify these with $H_1(L_{F/k})$ and $\Omega_{F/k}$. Transport scalars along the given $k$-algebra isomorphism $e:F\cong K$. The resulting coordinate map $\delta:K^c\to K^n$ and the transported kernel and cokernel isomorphisms are $K$-linear and give the claim. No dimension calculation or transcendence basis is used.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07E1, lines 8584-8592 (via Algebra Lemma 00S7, lemma-localize-NL, line 35692)

theorem exists_fractionField_completeIntersection_cotangent_model
    (k : Type u) (K : Type v) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (n : ℕ) (f : List (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))
    (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) f)
    [IsDomain (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ Ideal.ofList f)]
    (e : FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ Ideal.ofList f) ≃ₐ[k] K) :
    ∃ δ : (Fin f.length → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin n → K),
      Nonempty (H1Cotangent k K ≃ₗ[K] LinearMap.ker δ) ∧
      Nonempty (KaehlerDifferential k K ≃ₗ[K] ((Fin n → K) ⧸ LinearMap.range δ))
